## Step 1: Create the integration

1. Open WSO2 Integrator.
2. Select **Skip for now**.
3. Select **Create New Integration**.
4. Set **Integration Name** to `SetupGuide`.
5. Set **Project Name** to `microsoft-dynamics365-finance-receivable`.
6. Select **Create Integration**.
7. Select **SetupGuide**.

## Step 2: Register an application in Microsoft Entra ID

1. <!-- manual: Sign in to the [Azure portal](https://portal.azure.com/) and navigate to Microsoft Entra ID → App registrations → New registration. -->
2. Give the application a name (e.g., `d365-receivable-integration`), select the account type appropriate for your organization, and select **Register**.
3. <!-- manual: Give the application a name (e.g., d365-receivable-integration), select the account type appropriate for your organization, and select Register. -->
4. <!-- manual: On the application's Overview page, note the Application (client) ID and Directory (tenant) ID: both values are required by the connector. -->
5. Go to **Certificates & secrets → Client secrets → New client secret**, add a description and expiry, and select **Add**.
6. <!-- manual: add a description and expiry -->
7. <!-- manual: Copy the generated secret Value immediately: it is shown only once and is required by the connector as clientSecret. -->

## Step 3: Grant Dynamics 365 API permissions

1. <!-- manual: In the app registration, go to API permissions → Add a permission → APIs my organization uses. -->
2. <!-- manual: Search for Dynamics ERP (this is the service principal that represents your Dynamics 365 Finance & Operations environment) and select it. -->
3. Select **Application permissions**, then select the `user_impersonation` permission (or the equivalent scope exposed by your environment), and select **Add permissions**.
4. Select **Grant admin consent for `‹your tenant›`** and confirm.

## Step 4: Add the application as a Dynamics 365 Finance user

1. <!-- manual: In your Dynamics 365 Finance environment, go to System administration → Users → New. -->
2. <!-- manual: Set the User ID and User name, then in the Identity provider object ID (or Azure AD object ID) field, paste the Application (client) ID noted in Step 1. This links the app registration to a D365 user identity. -->
3. Assign the security roles required for the receivable entities you plan to work with (for example, **Accounts receivable clerk**, **Accounts receivable manager**, or **Credit and collections manager**) and save.
